title: Sony KV-1310 Trinitron
note: Sony's first Trinitron colour television (Japan, 1968): a walnut-grain cabinet with a carry handle, the screen on the left, a speaker and channel dial column on the right, and inside it the Trinitron picture tube (one gun, three beams, an aperture grille) on a transistor chassis. Frame: z up, cabinet bottom at z = 0, centred in x and y, the screen facing -y. Real size in metres. The cabinet's size is the Smithsonian's KV-1310; its layout comes from the Sony-owned set in the Japanese national registry (kahaku_00063, a photo we may measure from but not publish). The tube's construction is from Sony's 1967 patent and Belt (1972); its sizes are not yet found (open_questions).

identity.quote: Name (Model, etc.) Trinitoron color TV KV-1310 ... Manufacturer (Company) Sony Corporation Year Manufactured 1968

single_gun_three_beams.value: one electron gun, three beams side by side, crossing at the centre of one common focus lens; an aperture grille instead of a shadow mask
single_gun_three_beams.quote: Sony Corporation used a single-electron-gun-three-beam system and replaced the shadow mask with an aperture grille ... even when three beams cross over at a center of main lens of single electron gun, each beam shows a good focus on the phosphor screen

also.quote: a single electron gun emits a plurality of electron beams ... the beams are made to cross each other or intersect substantially at the optical center of electrostatic focusing lens common to all of the beams
The Trinitron emits three beams, one for each primary color, but from only one electron gun ... The beams in a Trinitron are side-by-side

cathodes.value: three separate cathodes; grid 1 common to all three (9- and 12-inch tubes)
cathodes.quote: In early Trinitrons - the 9- and 12-inch - only the cathodes are separate. Grid 1 is common to all three cathodes

beam_paths.value: the red and blue beams bend in, cross and fan out; the green beam runs straight; convergence plates steer the outer two back to cross again at the grille
beam_paths.quote: the red and blue beams bend, cross, and aim outward, while the green beam remains straight. As they pass between the convergence plates, the red and blue beams are directed back toward the center axis

convergence.value: electrostatic convergence plates in the neck, four neck magnets for static convergence, no convergence yoke
convergence.quote: Special plates converge Trinitron beams electrostatically ... Once mechanical (static) convergence is adjusted with four neck magnets

grille_and_phosphor.value: a grille of vertical slots; phosphor in narrow vertical stripes
grille_and_phosphor.quote: The Trinitron phosphor screen is deposited in narrow vertical stripes instead of tiny dots. (2) The mask behind the Trinitron phosphor is a grille of vertical slots

solid_state.value: transistor chassis: the picture tube is the set's vacuum tube
solid_state.quote: front panel label, read on the record's photo: "SOLID STATE | TRINITRON COLOR"

front_layout.value: walnut-grain wooden box with a black carry handle on top; a silver trim frame round the front; the screen in a black bezel on the left with a SONY plate under it; four knobs in a row below the screen; on the right a perforated speaker panel, a TRINITRON badge with red, green and blue bars, a COLOR plate and a rotary channel dial; PULL ON/VOL knob and two jacks at the bottom right; "SOLID STATE | TRINITRON COLOR" along the bottom; small feet
front_layout.quote: read on the record's photo (three-quarter view from front left)

value.material: mild steel sheet with etched vertical slits, stretched in a steel frame

aperture_grille.quote: 薄軟鋼板にエッチングで縦縞状の開口を作り,これを鋼枠に適当な張力を持たせた状態で架張したものである.軟鋼板は小型で0.1mm,大型で0.13mm ... グリルのピッチは小型で0.5〜0.6mm,大型で0.8mm前後であり,電子透過率は中心で20%
aperture_grille.note: 1973 figures for Trinitron tubes in general ('small' sizes), not stated for the 1968 KV-1310 tube

grille_dampers.value: fine wires stretched across the strips as vibration dampers; the frame's top and bottom edges L-section, held apart by two steel members
grille_dampers.quote: 各条に直交して振動のダンパーとしての細線を適当な張力で張って押えている ... 上下の辺はL形断面を有し ... 2本の鋼材eで支える構造である

face_shape.value: cylindrical: straight top to bottom, curved side to side
face_shape.quote: パネルは螢光面のY軸が直線に近く,X軸は適当なRを持った内面で構成され,円筒面として構成されたアパチャーグリルに対し

focus_voltage.value: 4-5 kV on the unipotential focus electrode; convergence plates' outer plates 0.4-1.5 kV below the gun's high voltage
focus_voltage.quote: ユニポテンシャルのフォーカス電極に中電圧の4〜5kVを印加する ... 偏向板の両外側の極板に電子銃の高圧電源よりも0.4〜1.5kV低い電圧を印加して

also.quote: Only a few hundred volts is needed.
also.note: conflicts: Belt writes of a few hundred volts for focus

boards_kv7010ua.quote: SIGNAL- DEFLECTION BOARD "SD" ... Chroma and Video Circuit Board "CV" ... POWER BOARD ... VOLTAGE REGULATOR BOARD ... N Circuit Board ... convergence board (OCR of the scanned manual)

line_period.quote: Table 1, System M: "Number of lines per picture (frame) 525", "Line frequency fH ... 15 750 (15 734.264"; line synchronizing signals, M: "Nominal line period (µs) 63.492 (63.5555)", "Line-blanking interval (µs) 10.2 to 11.4"; the bracketed values are the colour (NTSC) ones
line_period.note: System M is the 525-line, 60-field system of Japan and the US (the table's Japan footnotes sit under M)

beam_slowdown.quote: derived: one line in the Beam animation takes estimates.beam_animation line + retrace = 0.7 + 0.15 = 0.85 s; a real line takes 63.5555 µs (facts.line_period); 0.85 s / 63.5555 µs = 13,374, and the visible sweep alone 0.7 s / (63.5555 - 10.9) µs = 13,294; shown rounded as "≈13,000×"
beam_slowdown.note: only the sweep: the electrons' flight through the gun is slowed far more, and 12 lines stand in for 525

open_questions: Axes of the Smithsonian's 15 x 15 x 17 3/4 in: read here as height over the handle, depth and width (fits the kahaku photo's proportions). A front and a side photo of a KV-1310 would settle it; the cabinet heights of the KV-1310E (320 mm) and KV-1320UB (337 mm) are without handles and are later cabinets.

Screen size: 12-inch is what the sources say for the first sets (Science Museum: "This initial 12-inch model"; Belt: "the 9- and 12-inch"), but no source gives the KV-1310's tube type, its diagonal, neck diameter or length. The KV-1310E has a 330AB22 ("13\" (sichtbar 30,5 cm)"), the Science Museum's sectioned 1971 tube is a 330CB22. Until found, the tube is sized from the photo's screen opening and these figures stay estimates.

Aperture grille pitch, strip width, frame and any damper wires; cathode spacing and focus lens size: none found for the 1968 tube. The IEEE paper (Yoshida, Ohgoshi, Miyaoka, "The 'Trinitron' - A New Color Tube", IEEE Trans. BTR-14, July 1968) likely has them but wasn't obtained. Belt (1972) has the gun's layout, not its sizes.

Chassis layout: no KV-1310 manual or interior photo found. The chassis follows its sibling the KV-7010UA: the board list from its Sony service manual, the places from its Sams Photofact (SD and CV upright beside the tube, HV section with the 1S2/DY86 rectifier tube behind the tuners, power transformer below); sizes estimated.

Finishes (walnut grain, trim, bezel, knob colours): to be sampled from a photo. The only KV-1310 photo is kahaku_00063, which may not be reproduced; sampling colours from it is measuring, but no texture can be taken from it. A wood-grain texture would have to be made, not copied.

Photo licence: no openly licensed photo of a KV-1310 was found. The Commons photos are of the KV-1320UB (CC BY 4.0) and a 13-inch European set in Milan (CC BY-SA 4.0), both with different front panels.

The back: no KV-1310 back view found; the open wood sleeve and black plastic back cover follow the sibling KV-1320UB (Commons photo, CC BY 4.0), as estimates. The back's vents, aerial panel, switch, power socket and nameplate are laid out from the same photo (from_photos.back_layout).

Inside finishes (bulb glass, grille steel, gun metal, yoke copper) are estimated colours: no photo of a 1968 tube's inside found. The Science Museum's sectioned 1971 tube (co34468) photos are CC BY-NC-SA and weren't used.
